Every Hebrew run in the repaired rows passes normalize_hebrew_in_json.py (ok 44, fixed 0, defects 0) and each run in this row collates byte at its cited ref, so the defect is the claim made about the bytes, not the bytes.

Re-running the test that killed the original at the SEAM rather than at the field, tier-4 translation punctuation is still doing driver work at web:Ps.60.8|Ps.60.9 in the post-repair corpus, and the pair now argues one seam at two different evidence tiers, which is what the one-edit rule exists to prevent. The seam LOCATION is sound on both sides from the bytes above, tiling survives (60.6-8 | 60.9-12 | 61.1-4), M8-Ps-170 is not contradicted and the K/Q note at oshb:Ps.60.7 lies outside every quoted span — so the defect is the half-installed seam-pair cure, not the boundary.

Two items, both cured.
